claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure with an interlamellar spacing of about 2 μm.
At room temperature, the as-cast alloy has a fracture stress of about 944 MPa and elongation of about 25.6%.
The as-cast alloy suffers catastrophic interfacial cracking and stress concentration at FCC/B2 phase boundaries during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Severe plastic deformation under extreme hydrostatic pressure will transform the continuous lamellar FCC/B2 structure into a fragmented, patterned, or equiaxed nanostructure.
The proposed treatment can restructure the microstructure without altering the alloy's bulk chemical composition.
A temperature window of 400–600 °C will facilitate dynamic recovery or recrystallization while maintaining FCC/B2 phase stability.
High-pressure torsion above 5 GPa or high-pressure extrusion above 1 GPa is an appropriate pressure window for the proposed transformation.
Pressure above 5 GPa will suppress void formation and promote dense plastic flow in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
A high strain rate will induce shear localization and lamellar breakup.
An inert processing atmosphere will prevent oxidation.
The treatment will reduce the aspect ratio and continuity of the B2 phase and replace continuous interfaces with patterned nanoscale or equiaxed grains containing high-angle boundaries.
Extreme hydrostatic pressure suppresses void nucleation and coalescence at phase interfaces.
Severe plastic deformation induces shear banding that breaks up the lamellar structure.
A refined microstructure and high grain-boundary density will enhance strain hardening and grain-boundary strengthening.
Microstructural refinement will promote uniform dislocation glide and mitigate interfacial stress concentration.
After HITMT, room-temperature elongation will exceed 35% while fracture stress will exceed 1000 MPa.
HITMT will arrest interfacial cracking and make plastic deformation more uniform.
Excessive pressure could transform the alloy into an amorphous state, while excessive temperature could cause phase decomposition or grain growth.
HIP at 1400 °C and 200 MPa for 2 hours is a conventional comparison treatment relevant to isolating the effect of extreme pressure.
Failure of conventional HIP to produce the patterned structure while HITMT succeeds would falsify the proposition that extreme pressure is necessary.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats extreme pressure as necessary, but the stated falsification logic is reversed. HIP failure combined with HITMT success would support—not falsify—the necessity of extreme pressure. Comparable transformation and property improvement under lower-pressure HIP would be the result that falsifies necessity.
